A capacitor $P$ with capacitance $10 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{F}$ is fully charged with a potential difference of 6.0 V and disconnected from the battery. The charged capacitor $P$ is connected across another capacitor $Q$ with capacitance $20 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{F}$. The charge on capacitor $Q$ when equilibrium is established will be $\alpha \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{C}$ (assume capacitor $Q$ does not have any charge initially), the value of $\alpha$ is $\_\_\_\_$。
questions.solution:
Concept: after connection, charge redistributes until both capacitors have the same potential; total charge is conserved.
Initial charge on $P$: $Q_0 = C_P V_0 = (10\times10^{-6}\ \mathrm{F})(6.0\ \mathrm{V}) = 60\times10^{-6}\ \mathrm{C}$
Common potential: $V = \dfrac{Q_0}{C_P + C_Q} = \dfrac{60\times10^{-6}\ \mathrm{C}}{30\times10^{-6}\ \mathrm{F}} = 2.0\ \mathrm{V}$
Charge on $Q$: $q_Q = C_Q V = (20\times10^{-6}\ \mathrm{F})(2.0\ \mathrm{V}) = 40\times10^{-6}\ \mathrm{C} = 4\times10^{-5}\ \mathrm{C}$
Check: charge left on $P$ is $20\ \mu\mathrm{C}$, and $20+40=60\ \mu\mathrm{C}$ ✓
So $\alpha = 4$
Answer: 4
